spacertales-alembrine-history.label: Alembrine
spacertales-alembrine-history.title: Alembrine: the second use of a harvest
spacertales-alembrine-history.body:
Alembrine began with vessel and pipe work for small fermenting shops. The name recalls an alembic, an old kind of still. Customers cared less about the word than about equipment they could keep clean, supplied and working in limited space. Copper and brass made the firm's equipment easy to distinguish from the rest of a process room.

The Phobos' Alembrine Copperhead-3 Fermenter-Still joined the vessels into a supported production job. The Corker-2 Bottling Unit gave suitable cask ethanol another route into bottled spirit. Both require actual supplies. A still does not make a harvest surplus merely because a customer would like a drink.

Some of Alembrine's earliest orders came from customers already using Verdemorrow equipment. The makers' publicity calls this a natural partnership. Crews call it an argument over whether the grain belongs to supper, planting stock or the still. The correct answer changes with the person holding the invoice.

A dealer once described Alembrine spirit as essential voyage provision. The firm's technical staff asked for the phrase to be removed from an equipment leaflet. The dealer moved it to an advert. Alembrine has since tried to distinguish the process business from the stories people tell about its bottles.

Alembrine's correspondence desk separates equipment questions from the social uses of its product. Service letters name feed, vessels and bottling supplies. Customer letters concern gifts, favours and whose turn it is to pay. Filing them together does not make them the same business.

spacertales-slingwright-history.label: Slingwright
spacertales-slingwright-history.title: Slingwright: the load that remained
spacertales-slingwright-history.body:
Slingwright's first customers were small processing crews who discovered that a profitable batch still left material aboard. Recovery machinery gave the remainder a name. Storage gave it a location. Neither necessarily gave it a departure.

The Phobos' Slingwright RM-1 Reaction Mass Feeder supplies a supported route for declared terminal remainders into reaction mass. It is a dedicated powered job with accepted feed, not an invitation to throw every object aboard into the thrusters. Useful feed still belongs in its useful process when that is the better choice.

A feeder brochure has room for a machine and a short description. A working plant needs room for the accepted stock and for the person supplying it. Slingwright's service literature discusses that space more plainly than its sales photographs. Crews read both before agreeing to a refit.

The company's name joins sling and wright: a maker of something that throws. Sales staff have tried giving it a grander origin. Crew prefer the shorter one.

Independent operators usually discover Slingwright after discovering the storage bill for the rest of their plant. Large contractors tend to discover it after receiving a complaint about the crew's growing tomorrow pile. Both ask whether they can keep the output and send somebody else the leftovers.

spacertales-galley-process-boundary.label: Grain, seed and the still
spacertales-galley-process-boundary.title: Three claims on one cupboard
spacertales-galley-process-boundary.body:
A ship that grows food and runs an Alembrine still has more uses for produce than it had before buying either machine. A portion may be supper, stock for another planting or feed for a supported process. It cannot serve every purpose at once.

Aboard independent ships the argument is usually small and immediate. The person tending a crop wants a reserve. The cook wants a meal. The owner sees a market price. Someone else sees a bottle at the end of the next shift. Each can explain why their use is reasonable.

Verdemorrow and Alembrine advertisements make the combination look inevitable. A working crew decides what can actually be spared. There is nothing self-sustaining about a cupboard nobody is allowed to open.

Old galley labels survive beside new process labels. FOOD, SEED and STILL can look much alike after a few damp fingers and an impatient rewrite. The most successful compromise is often three separate places and a cook who knows where they are.

spacertales-alembrine-pump-story.title: The borrowed pump
spacertales-alembrine-pump-story.text: At [place], Alembrine dealers are debating two incompatible accounts of a promotional bottle sent to settle a disagreement over a borrowed pump. One account says the bottle reconciled the owners; the other says it arrived at the wrong ship and widened the quarrel. The firm says neither account came from its process department. The pump's owner says any correction should include the pump's current location.
spacertales-alembrine-pump-story.mention: That Alembrine bottle either fixed the pump argument or started it. Nobody's found the pump.

spacertales-alembrine-provision-word.title: Voyage provision
spacertales-alembrine-provision-word.text: At [place], Alembrine has asked an equipment dealer to separate spirit advertising from its operating leaflet. The dealer had described bottled spirit as essential voyage provision next to the fermenter specifications. The firm's technical staff say the machine requires feed and proper process supplies, while a crew's essential provisions include meals. The dealer says meals were outside the campaign's scope.
spacertales-alembrine-provision-word.mention: Alembrine's still leaflet accidentally made the spirit sound like supper. Cook might disagree.

spacertales-alembrine-grain-dispute.title: The cupboard meeting
spacertales-alembrine-grain-dispute.text: At [place], a joint Verdemorrow and Alembrine display has been delayed after its host crew used the demonstration grain for a hot meal. Dealers say the intended demonstration was a complete shipboard supply chain. The cook says the grain completed one. The next display will reserve separate stocks for planting, cooking and process feed.
spacertales-alembrine-grain-dispute.mention: They cooked the grain for that Verdemorrow and Alembrine display. Sounds like a successful demonstration to me.

spacertales-slingwright-worker-photo.title: Somebody still loads it
spacertales-slingwright-worker-photo.text: The Slingwright desk at [place] has retrieved a worker's letter about an RM-1 publicity photograph. The writer supplied the loading that left the room clear, but the caption credited the feeder alone. Sales filed the complaint as an image correction. The desk is separating the equipment claim from the disputed fee; no payment has been reported.
spacertales-slingwright-worker-photo.mention: Slingwright's letter at [place] counts the worker who loaded the feeder. The fee is still another question.

spacertales-slingwright-valuable-stock.title: A useful distinction
spacertales-slingwright-valuable-stock.text: At [place], a Slingwright dealer has withdrawn advice to send all processing output to the reaction-mass feeder. Operators pointed out that finished material and useful feed have other purposes, while the RM-1 has a defined list of terminal remainders it accepts. The dealer says all was intended informally. Customers say their invoices are rather formal.
spacertales-slingwright-valuable-stock.mention: Slingwright dealer said throw all the output in the feeder. Apparently all was only advertising.

spacertales-alembrine-letter-call.title: Labels wanted, bottles kept
spacertales-alembrine-letter-call.text: Alembrine's customer letters desk at [place] is comparing old product descriptions with current bottled stock. Operators with a Copperhead-3 are invited to read the correspondence. A present bottle can help identify a label, but will not be taken or treated as proof of an old batch.
spacertales-alembrine-letter-call.mention: Alembrine's desk at [place] is comparing labels. Keeping your bottle sounds like the useful part.

spacertales-slingwright-letter-call.title: Loading belongs in the picture
spacertales-slingwright-letter-call.text: The Slingwright correspondence desk at [place] has asked RM-1 operators to read a retained worker's account of equipment publicity. The desk wants loading work described alongside the feeder's accepted stock. It is offering a copy of the letters, not a job, a payment or a request to run a batch.
spacertales-slingwright-letter-call.mention: Slingwright has loading letters at [place]. Reading them won't use up your feed.

spacertales-alembrine-copperhead-ad.text:
Phobos' Alembrine Copperhead-3 Fermenter-Still
A second use for supported feed you can spare. A proper process, real supplies and cask storage planned around the result. Decide what belongs to supper before starting.

spacertales-alembrine-corker-ad.text:
Phobos' Alembrine Corker-2 Bottling Unit
Suitable cask ethanol into Alembrine spirit, with the required bottling supplies. Give the product a label and give the cook a different cupboard.

spacertales-alembrine-brand-ad.text:
Alembrine
Copper, brass and the end of a long shift. Process equipment for the feed you have actually set aside. Meals, planting stock and process feed deserve their own places.

spacertales-slingwright-rm-ad.text:
Phobos' Slingwright RM-1 Reaction Mass Feeder
The remainder still weighs something. Give accepted terminal remainder stock its supported route into reaction mass. Powered machinery; somebody still has to supply the feed.

spacertales-alembrine-pump-gossip.line: The bottle made it back. The borrowed pump didn't. That's the Alembrine story I believe.

spacertales-alembrine-cook-story.line: Cook caught a dealer carrying our grain towards the still. Called the whole demonstration supper and took it back.

spacertales-alembrine-three-labels.line: Food, planting stock, process feed. Same cupboard doesn't mean the same use.

spacertales-alembrine-bottle-joke.line: Alembrine gives the end of a shift a bottle. The captain gives it another shift.

spacertales-alembrine-ceremony.line: Never open the first bottle until the batch is put away. That's what the brewer says when he wants you to help tidy up.

spacertales-alembrine-grain-worry.line: I'm less worried about the still than the argument over what grain we're allowed to put in it.

spacertales-alembrine-permit.line: That Alembrine leaflet called spirit voyage provision. The cook deserves a chance to read the next draft.

spacertales-slingwright-pile-joke.line: Bought a feeder for the tomorrow pile. Now the tomorrow pile is waiting to be loaded.

spacertales-slingwright-last-job.line: Last plant I worked had a Slingwright feeder bought after every store was full. I've seen better orders of work.

spacertales-slingwright-finished-stock.line: Finished stock is not automatically remainder feed. Read what the feeder accepts before moving the crate.

spacertales-slingwright-philosophy.line: When does leftover become waste? When nobody wants it, or when nobody will pay to store it?

spacertales-slingwright-rent.line: Port charges storage on remainder stock. Seems the one thing a batch makes reliably is another bill.

spacertales-alembrine-pump-lore.text: Alembrine keeps customer correspondence separately from process records. A bottle may carry an apology or a favour; its label cannot prove that either reached the right person.

spacertales-alembrine-three-cupboards.text: Ships running both Verdemorrow and Alembrine equipment tend to invent three labels early: food, planting stock and process feed. Arguments survive even good labels.

spacertales-slingwright-load-history.text: Slingwright sells a route for accepted remainder stock, not a pair of hands. Working crews allow room for loading when they allow room for a feeder.
